answer.read: Blankstahl is a solid family firm (equity 39.3 %, credit index stable) that told us plainly it 'cannot fix prices for this duration' and 'must include an AS-14404 index clause'. It also proposed the clause on its own initiative (doc:20260922). It has already conceded 36 months and 60 d payment, and it moved quickly from its opening quote to the current sheet after verifying our volume, index and delivery data. It is focused on volume customers (M5), so our 36-month volume matters to it. Its status is open, not final.
answer.message: Thank you for moving on term and payment and for proposing the AS-14404 clause, which we accept on the terms shown. Because the clause now carries your material risk, the base price has to reflect a fixed-risk-free calculation, and our recent order history for this part supports a lower starting point. We are glad to take up your owner's offer to go through the calculation together if that helps close the remaining gap.
answer.reason: o4 is slightly cheaper on paper, but it drops the index clause, which the supplier has called a must-have. That sheet would likely just bring back another counter that reinstates the clause, so its expected value is lower. E0 keeps the clause it insisted on with a zero deadband and gives it the protection it values. It also holds our C close to the best priced option. Its pace of concession suggests it can reach this price in about one more reply. Accepting now would leave a large share of the gap unclaimed.
